name: application-table-error-state
title: Table Error State
description: In-table failure row: a normal table with a final row whose cell spans every column, showing a failure icon, reason, and a retry button in place of the remaining data.
useWhen: A table successfully loaded some rows but failed to load the rest (e.g. pagination or streaming failure) and needs an inline recovery affordance.
You want the error to read as part of the table's row structure rather than replacing the whole table or page.
Distinct from a generic Retry Error State, which fills an entire page or panel, rather than appearing as one row within an otherwise normal table.
avoidWhen: The entire table failed to load, with zero rows shown — a full-panel Retry Error State is more appropriate.
The table has no natural column structure to span — this pattern relies on colSpan across real columns.
responsiveBehavior: The error cell's colSpan always matches the live column count, so it continues to span the full table width if columns are added or removed.
accessibility: The failure icon is aria-hidden since the adjacent text conveys the same information.
Error title and message are both real text (not icon-only), and the Retry button has a clear text label rather than relying on an icon.

variants.title: Table Error State
variants.description: A table with two successfully loaded rows followed by a spanning error row showing a timeout message and a Retry button.
accessibility: Error icon is aria-hidden; title, message, and Retry button are all real text.

variants.title: Table Error State (Dark)
variants.description: The same table error row adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Icon and text contrast remain distinguishable at dark-surface contrast.
